title: Food, shopping & future plans
subtitle: Food, errands & plans
objectives: Make a practical request and confirm a price.
Use ir a plus infinitive for a plan.
Ask about an ingredient or available alternative.
warmup: Without notes, retrieve three phrases from Unit 10. Use each in a new situation, then explain one correction from your last quiz. If you cannot retrieve a phrase, review its card before starting this unit.

lectures.title: Requests that get useful answers
lectures.body: In a shop or café, begin with a greeting and use a clear noun phrase: Un café, por favor. Quisiera un café is a courteous learned expression meaning I would like a coffee; its full verb analysis comes later. ¿Me puede traer agua? is a polite request to one person. Ask ¿Cuánto cuesta? for one item and ¿Cuánto cuestan? for several. If the response is unclear, repeat the amount as a question. Do not practice by ordering things you do not want; a roleplay or a genuine small purchase can both serve a learning goal.

lectures.title: Plans with ir a
lectures.body: Use a conjugated form of ir, then a, then an infinitive: Voy a cocinar. Vamos a comprar pan. The action verb remains infinitive, not voy a cocino. Ir a also describes movement when followed by a destination: Voy al mercado. Distinguish the two by what follows a: an action or a place. Al combines a + el. For an upcoming plan, add mañana, esta tarde, or el sábado. This form is often called the near future, but its meaning is not restricted to a fixed number of hours or days.

lectures.title: Ingredients and preferences
lectures.body: Useful questions include ¿Qué lleva? (What is in it?), ¿Tiene leche? and ¿Hay una opción sin carne? Distinguish no me gusta from no puedo comer: a preference and a restriction are different messages. For an allergy, state it explicitly and confirm details; this course is not a guarantee that an interaction will be safe. Por favor, sin azúcar requests no sugar. Con means with, sin means without. Menú, carta, cuenta, and regional food names have context-dependent meanings. Ask what a local dish contains rather than assuming a familiar name means a familiar recipe.

reading:
—Buenas tardes. Quisiera un café, por favor.
—¿Con leche?
—Sin leche, gracias. ¿Cuánto cuesta?
—Dos euros.
—¿Y el bocadillo? ¿Qué lleva?
—Queso y tomate.
—Gracias. Hoy voy a comprar solo el café. Mañana vamos a cocinar en casa.
Identify the request, ingredient question, and two plans. Replace the currency and food with locally appropriate choices in your own roleplay.

task: Roleplay a café visit with an unavailable item. Ask about an alternative, confirm a price, then tell your partner your plan for tomorrow.
culture: Tipping, table service, vocabulary, and currencies differ widely. The dialogue uses euros as one example; Latin American practice uses many currencies and local food names. Learn the conventions of the actual place you visit.
selfAssessment: I can make a practical request and confirm a price.
I can use ir a plus infinitive for a plan.
I can ask about an ingredient or available alternative.
remediation: Group missed items by concept, not by score. Reread the relevant mini-lecture, explain one worked example aloud, and write two new examples. Rehearse the communication task after a day. If you can select an answer but cannot use it in an exchange, prioritize retrieval and partner practice.

quiz.prompt: Select the expression that communicates: I would like a coffee.
quiz.explanation: “Quisiera un café” communicates “I would like a coffee.” The other choices communicate “We are going to buy bread” and “Can you bring me water?”; those do not answer this prompt.

quiz.prompt: Select the expression that communicates: A coffee, please.
quiz.explanation: “Un café, por favor” communicates “A coffee, please.” The other choices communicate “I am going to the market” and “Just the coffee”; those do not answer this prompt.

quiz.prompt: Select the expression that communicates: How much does it cost?.
quiz.explanation: “¿Cuánto cuesta?” communicates “How much does it cost?.” The other choices communicate “Is there an option without meat?” and “Tomorrow”; those do not answer this prompt.

quiz.prompt: Select the expression that communicates: How much do they cost?.
quiz.explanation: “¿Cuánto cuestan?” communicates “How much do they cost?.” The other choices communicate “Can you bring me water?” and “I would like a coffee”; those do not answer this prompt.

quiz.prompt: Select the expression that communicates: What is in it?.
quiz.explanation: “¿Qué lleva?” communicates “What is in it?.” The other choices communicate “Just the coffee” and “A coffee, please”; those do not answer this prompt.

quiz.prompt: Select the expression that communicates: Without milk.
quiz.explanation: “Sin leche” communicates “Without milk.” The other choices communicate “Tomorrow” and “How much does it cost?”; those do not answer this prompt.

quiz.prompt: Match each English meaning to its Spanish expression. Use each expression once.
quiz.explanation: “¿Qué lleva?” means “What is in it?”. “Con azúcar” means “With sugar”. “Voy a cocinar” means “I am going to cook”. Each alternative belongs to a different meaning; check the whole phrase, including its grammatical person and register.

homework.prompt: Read the original text twice. Identify who is involved, the situation, and three key details. Rewrite it with two meaningful changes and underline the forms that had to change.
homework.model: Use the original text as a comparison model. Preserve its grammatical relationships, but change facts. Explain each changed ending using one of this unit’s mini-lectures.
homework.rubric: 0–2 each: accurate key details, coherent changes, target grammar, explanation of corrections. Maximum 8; self-assessment is not instructor validation.

homework.prompt: Listen to the original text using an available Spanish device voice or a willing reader. Hide the text, note five words or phrases you hear, then compare. Record the source and two uncertainties. If audio is unavailable, complete reading preparation and mark listening as not yet completed.
homework.model: A useful log includes source, date, words actually heard, and a correction confirmed against the text. Synthetic speech is listening rehearsal and does not represent the range of natural accents.
homework.rubric: 0–2 each: documented source, specific notes, comparison, actionable next step. Score the process; do not invent comprehension evidence.

homework.prompt: Roleplay a café visit with an unavailable item. Ask about an alternative, confirm a price, then tell your partner your plan for tomorrow.
homework.model: Use the dialogue or reading for a model of suitable language, then change the facts. Include one request for clarification and a response to it. Save your recording or a written interaction reflection.
homework.rubric: 0–3 each: task completion, comprehensibility, target-form control, responsiveness. A 3 means independently effective for this task; 2 some help; 1 frequent help; 0 no evidence. Mark solo work as rehearsal.

homework.prompt: After at least one day, produce five flashcard phrases without looking. Use two in new sentences. Compare with your earlier work and write one concrete plan for the next study session.
homework.model: Example reflection format: I retrieved [phrase], but confused [form]. I will revisit [lecture] and use the corrected form in [specific situation].
homework.rubric: Count successful retrieval separately from task quality. A useful reflection names an error, a correction, and a new use.
